title: Exact derived adjunctions: lower bounds, reflection and counits
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories with derived categories, F:A→B an exact additive functor and FD:D(A)→D(B) a functor equipped with Q_A FD≅F_complex Q_B. Then (1) if FD is left adjoint to RD, RD preserves every standard cohomological lower bound; (2) if FD is faithful on morphisms between bounded-below objects, it reflects isomorphisms on the entire unbounded derived category; (3) if FD is fully faithful on morphisms between bounded-below objects, then the counit is invertible at any object isomorphic to FD(X) for bounded-below X. The hypotheses in (2) and (3) concern all pairs of bounded-below objects, with possibly different bounds.

proof.text: Localization identifies FD with the standard mapDerivedCategory of F, which commutes with cohomology and both standard bounds. Orthogonality and the adjunction show that RD preserves each lower bound.

Degree-zero single functors are fully faithful. Restricting the bounded-below faithfulness assumption to them makes F faithful. A faithful functor between abelian categories is conservative; use the homology comparison and homology detection to reflect arbitrary derived isomorphisms.

For bounded-below X, both X and RD(FD(X)) are bounded below. The adjunction and assumed bijections make postcomposition with the unit bijective on the Hom sets from both objects. Obtain a two-sided inverse of the unit. The triangle identity makes the counit at FD(X) invertible, and counit naturality transports this to any isomorphic object.
